### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/formula`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838`.

⛔ **8** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/formula/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd538ffd21f3b0528f5097a9d314bc4581315961` — the merge of head `7917005afdcb6a3a2db3a3a204f0605679890d13` into base `93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd538ffd21f3b0528f5097a9d314bc4581315961 && git checkout cd538ffd21f3b0528f5097a9d314bc4581315961
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838 7917005afdcb6a3a2db3a3a204f0605679890d13 && git checkout -B drift-repro 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838 && git merge --no-ff 7917005afdcb6a3a2db3a3a204f0605679890d13

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 93b4acb57ec23c4e94a7047133ce612f89a13838` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e9c02e68133e6f68004af8682a6c07369e517250`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.ts, packages/formula/src/validate.ts, packages/formula/src/index.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-formula-one-hop.test.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.formula-one-hop.test.ts, packages/formula/src/relationship-traversal.test.ts, packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx + packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts, packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts, packages/objectql/src/index.ts, packages/objectql/src/core.ts, packages/objectql/package.json, packages/spec/src/data/field-value.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts, packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/*.object.ts (formula census), content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx, scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs, scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs

Inputs: card #24197 (its body with the `Ruled:` line; comments 6237225524, 6238165661, 6245950717, 6245997444, 6247217617), PR #24274 (body, the 17-file list, the one docs-drift comment, no review comments or reviews), the net diff `origin/main...e9c02e6813` (merge base 53ef752436, +1074/−68) read with `git show` and `git diff`, and the head's check-runs. The merge base of this diff differs from origin/main (93b4acb57e) only by main's own later commits; the three-dot diff was taken after a fresh fetch.

Check-runs at read time (2026-10-18T07:53:58Z): 39 runs. 27 completed success, among them Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Build Core, Build Docs, every Lint job (CI/release/engine gates, ESLint, PM dispatch-gates, docs and code guards, repo and tooling gates, the three scoped jobs), Type Check source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Spec property liveness, Dogfood Regression Gate, and the three claim and card guards. 5 skipped by design (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance, Packed-tarball smoke). 7 still in progress and not waited on: Test Core 1/6 to 6/6 and Type Check · workspace. Those seven are the gate verdict on the new pins and the moved loader; this record does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

Judged against the `Ruled:` line verbatim: "The formula read path preloads one hop of the referenced fields a formula names (page-batched, as validation rules do); lint admits one hop and refuses two; a title formula over lookups sorts and searches by its stored value or is declared unsortable — written as an ADR-0079 note."

1. The read path preloads one hop — RIGHT. `planFormulaProjection` plans `hops` per formula off `collectReferenceTraversals`, which is `collectPredicateRelationships`'s own inlined `addFrom` moved verbatim into `addReferenceTraversals` (dialect check, `referenceTargetOf` filter, the same fold). `applyFormulaPlan` evaluates each traversing formula against a per-formula shallow copy whose reference slot holds the related row, so the row the read returns keeps the foreign key (pinned). Served on `find`, `findOne`, and the insert and update responses: `hydrateWriteFormulas` gained `relatedFor`, and both of its call sites (insert, update) pass it. Fields typed `lookup`, `master_detail`, `user` (implicit `sys_user`) and a registry-materialised `tree` self-reference all traverse, because both seams ask `referenceTargetOf`.

2. Page-batched, one read per reference field per page — RIGHT. `resolveFormulaRelated` folds the plan's hops into one `wanted` map and calls `resolveOneHopRelated` once over the page the driver returned (after limit and offset); the loader issues one `find` per reference field with `where id $in [the page's distinct FKs]` and `fields [id, ...named]`, never one per row (pinned: four loans over three books and two readers make one book read and one reader read; the second page reads only its own ids; a projection naming only the formula is widened for the read and cut back). A plan with no hop costs nothing (`wanted.size === 0` returns before any closure or query); a `hopConflict` entry asks for nothing. The traversal analysis is memoised (`analysisFor`, capped cache). Bound: the distinct FKs of the page the caller asked for. The engine fills no default `limit` (`fillQueryAstDefaults` parses orderBy and expand only; the spec's `limit` carries no default), so a direct `find` with no `limit` makes one `$in` over every distinct FK of the whole result; REST callers are bounded by their page. The related read carries no `limit`, so it is never truncated.

3. "As validation rules do" — RIGHT on the mechanism, and RIGHT to diverge on authority. The diff of `resolvePredicateRelated` at the merge base against `resolveOneHopRelated` at the head is exactly: the referential-clear guard and `collectPredicateRelationships` stay in the wrapper; `bound` becomes `authority === 'predicate' && !isSystem`; the hop query's context is the caller's when `authority === 'caller'` and `{ ...context, isSystem: true }` otherwise; the `WeakSet` marker is added for `caller` only; the warn wording branches. Nothing else moves, so for `authority: 'predicate'` the validation path's behaviour (SYSTEM behind the caller's read doors, the master-detail header door, the federated and no-tenant own-read, the walled no-tenant readsNothing) is unchanged — proven by the diff, not asserted. The formula arm reads as the CALLER through the public `find` (RLS composition at the ADR-0139 boundary, the middleware chain, the FLS result mask, the organization wall, the related object's own hooks), which is the right authority for data handed to a reader. A related row the caller's read does not return is `unresolved`, and the refusal sentence names neither "missing" nor "hidden" (pinned: the hidden reader's name is absent from the response; SYSTEM reads it).

4. Refusals at read time — RIGHT. Not found or not readable → `unresolved`; the related object declares no such field → `undeclared-field`; the read threw (a PERMISSION_DENIED from the middleware included) → `unreadable`. Each leaves the formula UNEVALUATED: `null` plus the reason to the fault sink, so no optional read can turn a missing or hidden record into the author's fallback (pinned: a dangling `b_gone` with `.?name.orValue('—')` reads null). An EMPTY reference is evaluated against the stored empty value; a plain read through it faults and the fault names `record.FIELD.?RELATED.orValue('…')`. The fault sink stays `logger.warn`, once per (object, field) per engine instance; nothing of it reaches the response. On every read path examined (find, findOne, the list route through find, insert and update responses) a formula discloses nothing the caller could not read directly; the by-name meta read returns metadata and evaluates no formula.

5. Lint admits one hop and refuses two — RIGHT. `judgeFieldFormula` passes `traversalHydration: true` for a formula `expression`, the only `value`-role opt-in at this head (the `check` helper passes the flag on rule conditions only, as before). `validateExpression` honours the flag for `value` with `subject: 'formula'`, through the same `readRootMembers` analyser and the same `REFERENCE_VALUE_TYPES` arbiter as the predicate arm. One hop passes, as it already did; `record.book.shelf.code` is refused `traversal-multi-hop` with the formula wording and no rule-shaped repair; the metadata save door runs this pass, so an active save answers 422 INVALID_METADATA (measured in the report; a draft save defers to promotion as before). Callers that do not pass the flag see no change (pinned).

6. The bare-and-traversed refusal (`record.reader == null ? '—' : record.reader.name`) — RIGHT, though beyond the ruling's words; see ③.1. It is the validation path's own second unserviceable shape, judged by the one `findTraversalConflicts`, and the engine refuses it at plan time (`hopConflict`), so metadata that never met the lint reads null WITH the same sentence.

7. Sort and search — RIGHT, and pre-existing. `assertOrderByIsMaterializable` (engine; present at the merge base, line 1822 there) throws `INVALID_SORT` 400 for a formula in `orderBy` on `find` and `findOne`; the REST door's `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` (protocol.ts line 13429 at the merge base) throws `INVALID_FIELD` 400 for a `searchFields` entry naming a virtual field; `resolveSearchFieldResolution`'s auto-default admits textual and enum types only, so a formula is never in it, and `isVirtualSearchField` drops a declared one. The PR touches none of these files; it only pins the engine sort refusal. The ruling's third limb therefore resolves to "declared unsortable and unsearchable", written into the four describe strings; the ADR-0079 note is the follow-up Tier H PR, as the claim says.

8. Public surface. `@objectstack/objectql`: `collectReferenceTraversals` and `referenceTraversalConflicts` are exported from the module file but from neither `index.ts` nor `core.ts`, and the package's `exports` map has `.` and `./core` only, so they are NOT published; `evaluateFormulaField` keeps its signature. `@objectstack/formula`: `findTraversalConflicts` gains an optional fourth parameter `subject`, and `TraversalSubject` is a NEW exported type on the package index — an additive widening of a published surface. `@objectstack/lint`: no export moves. `@objectstack/spec`: four describe strings, no shape change; `content/docs/references/ai/solution-blueprint.mdx` is the regenerated output and matches them.

9. The declaration. `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is RIGHT on the narrowing limb and WRONG on the widening limb: by `clause2-line.mjs`'s own table, a diff that widens one published surface (item 8, the formula index) and narrows another is `yes (narrowing)`. No gate reads differently (the level axis stands down on `no`, and every moved package is already graded `minor`), and the tier served here is the higher one either way, so this is a declaration defect, not a contract defect: the adopting seat corrects the PR body line and `.changeset/24197-formula-traversal-subject.md`'s line to `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`.

10. What saved yesterday and is refused today (the narrowing an author meets): a formula `expression` that reads two hops, or a reference both bare and traversed. Before: the active save answered 200, every row read `null`, and one warn line named an evaluator fault (`No such key`). After: the active save answers 422 with the located prescription; a row stored before still reads `null`, with the lint's sentence in the warn instead of the evaluator's. Nothing that computed a value stops computing. In-repo census at the head: 37 formula builders across examples, platform objects, plugins and services, none reading through a reference (the eight `display_title` formulas compose stored ids); no example, seed or fixture is refused. `content/docs/data-modeling/formulas.mdx` line 104 already teaches the one-hop composed title `record.customer.name`, false at the merge base and true at this head; no doc teaches a two-hop formula.

11. The flipped pin and the two gate-forced rows — RIGHT. `relationship-traversal.test.ts`'s "checks nothing in the `value` role" asserted the old accept set and now asserts the refusal's code, params and wording plus the opted-out control; `federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` renames three ledger keys to the moved function names with unchanged dispositions and adds the `referenceTraversalConflicts :: referenceTargetOf()` row; `system-context.mdx` row 29b moves its anchor to `resolveOneHopRelated` for the census gate.

### ② Semver level

Four changesets, read against the diff and `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (launch window: a breaking change ships `minor` with a BREAKING carrier and an ADR-0087 marker; `major` refused). The `Check Changeset` check-run is success, which is CI's verdict.

- `@objectstack/formula` `minor` — right. Additive public surface (an optional parameter, a new exported type) is at least `minor`; the opted-in `value` narrowing is breaking for opt-in callers only, carried by the `feat(formula)!:` summary and the `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker. "Without the flag, every role behaves as before" is true at this head.
- `@objectstack/lint` `minor` — right. An accept-set narrowing (two refused shapes), breaking by the narrowing convention; `!` summary plus marker; a "What to do" line present.
- `@objectstack/objectql` `minor` — right. Public methods change behaviour (a hop computes; two shapes read null with a reason); no export moves; `!` summary plus marker; "What to do" present. Its "a related field it may not see reads as empty" is accurate: an FLS-masked related column is materialised `null` by the loader.
- `@objectstack/spec` `patch` — right. Describe strings only; no shape, key or export moves; it carries no Clause-② line, correctly, since it narrows nothing.

Correction owed on the declaration, not the level: the PR body and the formula changeset read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`; the honest reading is `yes (narrowing)` (①.9). No bump moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. Refusing a reference read both bare and traversed (open question 1, shipped A). Answered: within the ruling's "as validation rules do". It is the validation path's own second shape, judged by the one `findTraversalConflicts`, and the null test an author writes today reads null anyway at the merge base (the traversal faulted on the stored id), so no working formula is removed. The prescribed `record.reader.?name.orValue('—')` is itself a one-hop read and is pinned on both seams. The ADR-0079 note must state the refusal; the carried `adr_note_text` does.

2. Evaluating an empty reference (open question 2, shipped A). Answered: right. A dangling or hidden record is never evaluated, so the author's fallback cannot stand in for a record that is missing or withheld (pinned). One consequence to record, not to change: an FLS-masked related column is materialised `null`, so an optional read answers the author's fallback for it exactly as for an empty column — FLS's posture everywhere (masked reads as absent), disclosing nothing.

3. Depth one and the cycle guard (open question 3, shipped A). Answered: right; the ruling fixes the depth, and the report's ablation showed non-termination without the guard. Mechanism note for the owning seat: the guard is a `WeakSet` keyed on the hop query object and read back inside `find` after `foldEngineOptionAliases` and `lowerWhereFilterArray`; both return the caller's own object when nothing folds (verified at the head: no alias key on the hop query, an object `where`, and copy-on-write comparand normalisation that returns the input unless a comparand is narrowed), so the identity holds at this head and the ping/pong pin guards it. A future normaliser that copies, or a numeric primary key whose string `$in` comparands get narrowed, would drop the marker silently, and the pin is the only thing that would catch it; a comment at the `find` call site naming the dependency is cheap.

4. A member read through a non-reference field (open question 4, shipped A). Answered: right. `referenceTargetOf` is the arbiter on both seams, so `record.address.city` on an object-valued field is not planned as a hop and keeps traversing. Note: `user` and `tree` fields ARE references and traverse; the describe strings and the carried ADR note text say "lookup / master_detail" — an under-statement, not a false claim; the ADR note should say "a reference field (lookup, master_detail, user, tree)".

5. The two gate-forced rows outside the claim. Both right and mechanical. Row 29b's prose still describes the predicate authority's elevation while its anchor now names a function carrying two authorities; the census gate checks the anchor only. Suggest the row name `authority: 'predicate'` in a later docs pass; not blocking.

6. The carried `adr_note_text`. True of this code in every clause but one. "it is shown on every surface" is NOT true at this head: `evaluateFormulaField` (synchronous, preloads no hop; the PR names it as such) is what `resolveRecordTitle` (`packages/objectql/src/record-title.ts`) runs, and `resolveRecordTitle` is the hook-body title accessor `ctx.title()` in `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts`. A composed title over lookups — the card's own producer case — answers `undefined` there while every REST read now shows it. ESCALATED: either the ADR note carves out the hook-body title accessor by name, or a card closes it (resolve the title over the engine's read, or hand the hook the record the read path already materialised). The report's "noted, not filed" is below Prime Directive #10 for a surface the ADR note would advertise; the adopting seat files it (dedupe words: `ctx.title` formula hop; `resolveRecordTitle` one hop; `evaluateFormulaField` traversal null).

7. The out-of-scope finding: `?search=zzzz` on an object whose fields are two lookups and a formula title answers every row. REAL at this head and INDEPENDENT of this PR. At the merge base, `resolveSearchFieldResolution` (`packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts`) auto-admits textual and enum types only, so lookup and formula are out; `expandSearchToFilter` (`packages/objectql/src/search-filter.ts`, `if (searchFields.length === 0) return null`) then hands `expandSearchOnAst` no filter, `where` is untouched and the term is dropped; the REST door's `assertSearchFieldsAreSearchable` fires only on an explicit `searchFields`, never on a bare `search` over an empty allowed set. Neither file is in this diff. A public-door wrong answer (class a); a dedupe over the titles of the 1,200 most recent issues found no card (#6674 and #24087 are neighbours, not duplicates). The adopting seat files it; the direction is the #4254 posture: an unhonoured search is a 400, never a silent widening.

8. Reviewer's own flags, none blocking:
   a. Log volume: a caller lacking read on the related object makes `resolveOneHopRelated`'s `catch` log a `warn` on every page read (once per `find` per reference field), and that warn is not deduped the way `reportFormulaFault` is. Suggest treating a PERMISSION_DENIED as a quiet `unreadable`, or deduping per (object, field).
   b. FLS on the carrying object's own FK column does not stop the hop: formulas compute before the middleware post-phase, as for any own column a formula reads today, so a formula can show a related name whose FK the caller may not see. A pre-existing posture extended, not a new one; the control is FLS on the formula field itself. Worth one sentence in the ADR note.
   c. The hop read fires the related object's `beforeFind` and `afterFind` hooks and its middleware once per page, as the caller — expected, and auditable as the caller's own read.
   d. `hydrateWriteFormulas` has exactly two call sites (insert, update) at the merge base and at the head; bulk write responses computed no formula before and compute none now. No change; noted for completeness.
   e. Seven check-runs were in progress at read time (preamble); the adopting seat reads their conclusions before the queue.
